title: Enhance governance with metadata enforcement rules in Amazon SageMaker
key_points: SageMaker Catalog can require filled-in metadata forms before an asset is published or before a subscription request is sent, set per domain unit.
The collected request metadata can drive custom approval or automatic fulfilment outside SageMaker.
Small governance launch; pairs with the Nov 2026 compliance-scoring post.
services: Amazon SageMaker Catalog, Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio
decision: Optional metadata with later audits vs enforced metadata at publish and request time
authors: Amazon Shipping Tech — Pradeep Misra, Ramesh H Singh, Sandhya Edupuganti

title: Build multi-Region resilient Apache Kafka applications with identical topic names using Amazon MSK and Amazon MSK Replicator
key_points: MSK Replicator can copy topics to a cluster in another Region under the same names, so clients fail over by switching bootstrap servers without renaming topics.
Walks through an active-passive setup, monitoring replication lag, failover to the secondary Region, and failback by replicating in the other direction.
Replication is asynchronous, so consumers may see duplicates after failover and downstream writes should be idempotent.
decision: Single-Region Kafka vs active-passive vs active-active replication, and identical vs prefixed topic names, for streaming disaster recovery

title: Using Amazon S3 Tables with Amazon Redshift to query Apache Iceberg tables
key_points: Getting-started path for Redshift Serverless reading Iceberg tables in S3 Tables: create a table bucket, turn on the analytics integration, define a database and table in Lake Formation, load rows with Athena.
The table bucket appears in Redshift through an auto-mounted catalog, so it is queried with ordinary SQL and no external schema; Redshift's service role needs read-only Lake Formation admin.
Read-only at the time; later posts add Redshift writes and transactions on Iceberg.
services: Amazon Redshift Serverless, Amazon S3 Tables, Apache Iceberg, AWS Lake Formation, Amazon SageMaker Lakehouse, Amazon Athena
decision: Load lake data into Redshift managed storage vs query Iceberg in S3 Tables in place from Redshift
attaches_to: dbt-pipelines (Athena + Iceberg folder; Redshift Serverless reading S3 Tables)

title: Connect, share, and query where your data sits using Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio
key_points: A business team in SageMaker Unified Studio finds, requests and gets approved access to customer files in S3, sales history in Redshift and a product catalog in DynamoDB, then joins them in one query without copying data.
Shows the publish, subscribe, approve and fulfil cycle, and how federated sources appear as catalog assets.
Long console walkthrough; the value is seeing how a catalog-driven access request works end to end.
services: Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio, Amazon SageMaker Catalog, Amazon SageMaker Lakehouse, Amazon Redshift, Amazon DynamoDB, Amazon Athena
decision: Copy data into one store vs catalog subscription with federated queries across S3, Redshift and DynamoDB

title: Introducing vector search with UltraWarm in Amazon OpenSearch Service
key_points: OpenSearch k-NN indexes can now move to the cheaper UltraWarm and Cold tiers, with three sizing scenarios showing where tiering saves money.
Vector-search storage feature, off the reader's path.
authors: Kunal Kotwani, Sorabh Hamirwasia, Navneet Verma

title: Build a data lakehouse in a hybrid Environment using Amazon EMR Serverless, Apache DolphinScheduler, and TiDB
key_points: Copies data from an on-premises TiDB warehouse to S3 (full dumps, checkpointed incremental dumps or a CDC connector), processes it in layers with EMR Serverless, and orchestrates the jobs with Apache DolphinScheduler.
Built around niche third-party tools; the reader's own CDC and orchestration bytes are better served elsewhere.
services: Amazon EMR Serverless, Apache DolphinScheduler, TiDB, Amazon Athena, AWS Glue Data Catalog

title: Implement Amazon EMR HBase Graceful Scaling
key_points: Scripts to move regions off and decommission HBase region servers on EMR before scale-in, and to stop region servers starting on Spot task nodes.
HBase operations, off the reader's path.
authors: Yu-Ting Su, Chris Li, Hsing-Han Wang, Cheng Wang

title: Architect fault-tolerant applications with instance fleets on Amazon EMR on EC2
key_points: Reduces EMR capacity failures by reserving baseline capacity with On-Demand Capacity Reservations and covering spikes with flexible instance fleets, prioritised allocation, subnet choice and managed scaling.
EMR-on-EC2 capacity planning, off the reader's main path.
services: Amazon EMR, Amazon EC2 Capacity Reservations
authors: Deepmala Agarwal, Flavio Torres, Suba Palanisamy

title: Deploy real-time analytics with StarTree for managed Apache Pinot on AWS
key_points: Partner piece contrasting self-managed Apache Pinot with StarTree's managed service for low-latency analytics on Kafka or Kinesis streams: security, ingestion, tiered storage and upserts.
Vendor positioning, off the reader's path.
services: Apache Pinot, StarTree, Amazon MSK, Amazon Kinesis Data Streams
authors: StarTree — Raj Ramasubbu, Francisco Morillo, Ismail Makhlouf, Mayank Shrivastava and Barkha Herman, Renee Berry

title: Announcing end-of-support for Amazon Kinesis Client Library 1.x and Amazon Kinesis Producer Library 0.x effective January 30, 2026
key_points: KCL 1.x and KPL 0.x went into maintenance in April 2025 and lost support on 30 January 2026; non-Java KCL wrappers are affected too, and migration guides point to KCL 3.x and KPL 1.x.
The deadline has passed, so this is only a reminder to check for old consumer libraries.
services: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams, Kinesis Client Library, Kinesis Producer Library

title: Accelerate analytics and AI innovation with the next generation of Amazon SageMaker
key_points: General-availability announcement for SageMaker Unified Studio: one environment combining EMR, Glue, Athena, Redshift, Bedrock and SageMaker AI tools, with SageMaker Catalog governance and Lakehouse data access.
Leadership overview with no technical depth.
services: Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio, Amazon SageMaker Lakehouse, Amazon SageMaker Catalog

title: Develop and test AWS Glue 5.0 jobs locally using a Docker container
key_points: AWS publishes a Glue 5.0 Docker image so Glue PySpark jobs can be written and run on a laptop with spark-submit, an interactive shell, pytest or VS Code, using local AWS credentials.
Lists what changed from the Glue 4.0 image and how to add JDBC drivers, extra Python packages, Livy/JupyterLab and a local Spark history server for debugging.
A cheap way to unit-test Glue code before paying for job runs; check for an image matching the current Glue version.
services: AWS Glue, Docker, Apache Spark, pytest
decision: Develop Glue jobs against the cloud (notebooks, test runs) vs locally in the Glue Docker image with unit tests
attaches_to: aws-bytes: Data Quality Check (done) and other Glue bytes (local test setup)

title: Enhancing Adobe Marketo Engage Data Analysis with AWS Glue Integration
key_points: Glue gained a native connector for Adobe Marketo Engage, so marketing leads and activities can be pulled with a visual Glue Studio job instead of custom API code.
Setup: store OAuth credentials in Secrets Manager, create a Glue connection, build a job that writes to S3, then query in Athena.
One early example of Glue's SaaS connector catalogue, which later grew much larger.
services: AWS Glue, AWS Glue Studio, Amazon Athena, AWS Secrets Manager, Adobe Marketo Engage
decision: Native Glue SaaS connector vs AppFlow vs custom API ingestion for marketing-platform data
authors: Adobe — Kenny Rajan, Kamen Sharlandjiev, Basheer Sheriff, Rafal Pawlaszek

title: Unlock the power of optimization in Amazon Redshift Serverless
key_points: Instead of a fixed base RPU, a Serverless workgroup can be given a price-performance target on a five-step slider; Redshift then learns the workload and adjusts base and scaled capacity itself.
AWS reports the feature suits workloads that would otherwise need roughly 32 to 512 base RPUs, and advises measuring a baseline first from query-history and serverless-usage system views.
AWS reports that on a 3 TB TPC-DS concurrent test, Balanced ran about twice as fast as cost-optimised for about 3% more cost, and performance-optimised about four times as fast for about 19% more.
decision: Fixed base RPU vs AI-driven price-performance target (cost, balanced, performance) for a Serverless workgroup
attaches_to: dbt-pipelines (Redshift Serverless workgroup settings); aws-bytes: cost optimization (later)
authors: Ricardo Serafim, Andre Hass, Milind Oke

title: Express brokers for Amazon MSK: Turbo-charged Kafka scaling with up to 20 times faster performance
key_points: Introduces MSK Express brokers: Kafka-compatible brokers with storage managed by AWS, preset best-practice settings and no disk sizing, so scaling is mostly about adding brokers.
AWS reports up to 3x the throughput per broker, up to 20x faster scaling and up to 90% faster recovery than Standard brokers, plus a worked scaling example and best practices.
Baseline reading for the later Express posts (in-place upgrades, Graviton4 M8g, S3 delivery) already in the radar.
decision: Standard brokers with self-sized storage vs Express brokers for Kafka clusters that must scale quickly

title: Build a secure data visualization application using the Amazon Redshift Data API with AWS IAM Identity Center
key_points: The Redshift Data API now accepts single sign-on with trusted identity propagation, so a custom app can run queries as the signed-in corporate user instead of one shared service login.
Example: a Streamlit sales dashboard behind Okta and IAM Identity Center on Redshift Serverless, where role-based row- and column-level rules show each regional manager only their region.
Walks through the token exchange step by step (IdP token, Identity Center token, identity-enhanced role session), which is the fiddly part to get right.
services: Amazon Redshift, Redshift Data API, Amazon Redshift Serverless, AWS IAM Identity Center, Okta, Streamlit
decision: Shared service user with app-side filtering vs per-user identity propagation with warehouse row-level security for custom data apps
authors: Songzhi Liu, Fei Peng, Rohit Vashishtha, Yanzhu Ji

title: Cross-account data collaboration with Amazon DataZone and AWS analytical tools
key_points: Console walkthrough: a producer account owns a DataZone domain, associates a consumer account, publishes Glue and Redshift tables to the catalog, and the consumer subscribes and queries them from Athena and the Redshift query editor.
The same flow now lives in SageMaker Unified Studio; the cross-account sharing idea is better covered by later lakehouse and governance posts.
services: Amazon DataZone, AWS Glue Data Catalog, Amazon Redshift, Amazon Athena, AWS Lake Formation
authors: Arun Pradeep Selvaraj, Piyush Mattoo, Mani Yamaraja

title: Amazon OpenSearch Service vector database capabilities revisited
key_points: Year-in-review of OpenSearch vector features: hybrid lexical plus semantic search with dense and sparse vectors, accuracy tuning, quantization and disk mode for cost, and simpler model connectors and chunking.
Search-platform roundup, off the reader's path.
